non_peer_source_records.reason: Only memorial narration for a fallen Marmola warrior: no direct voice and no durable behavior beyond fighting fiercely and dying; useful as contextual funeral/battle lore for Othon and Bari, not as a scene persona.
Non-peer lore fact bundle: two unnamed daughters act as a paired group; Honcho peer cards must represent one character, not a plural unit.
Title/mystery hook for a scar origin in the frame narrative, not a distinct Honcho peer character.
This is a duplicate title/alias-style singleton for the reigning Empress who appeals to Steelhead; the usable persona belongs on the existing Empress peer rather than a separate base card.
Single source-thin advising-intelligence hook with one contextual action directing Steelhead to Terra Prima; no durable voice, behavior, or scene-usable persona beyond Steelhead's love-quest lore.

Source is an object/dynastic-crest reference: the Castaka crest contains circuitry used in explaining Steelhead/Melmoth's body, with no distinct actor, voice, behavior, or relationships to support a peer persona.

Recap-only title/office record with no distinct personal voice or scene behavior; its useful evidence is the TechnoCardinal/Technoclergy ultimatum already better supported by the fuller Immaculate Techno Cardinal and Don Nicanor clone records.

Metacraft is a voice-interfaced spacecraft/technology record, not a distinct peer persona; its usable evidence is craft capability and command context for the Supreme Metabaron and Tonto, and a card would require inventing sentience or traits beyond the source.

One-page unidentified deathbed figure with no durable behavior, traits, or reusable scene voice; the record mainly preserves contextual birth/lineage evidence around Aghora and the uncertain Klezea/Klezra reference.
One-page named traitor/opponent with uncertain visual identity, no voice, traits, relationships, or durable behavior; evidence mainly contextualizes Aghora's executioner/prison combat lore.
One-line named opponent/prisoner record with no voice, relationships, durable behavior, or scene-usable persona; its value is contextual evidence for Aghora's Khaliyuga executioner assignment.

Source evidence treats Bushitaka as a narration-cited combat doctrine/authority label, not a distinct actor with voice, behavior, or scene presence; its value is contextual lore for Aghora's strike.

Unnamed one-page prophecy claimant whose only durable value is contextual scene lore for the conspiracy against the Empress and the dark-haired warrior's dismissal; a base card would require inventing personality beyond the claim.
Deceased, voiceless, and not physically depicted; the record exists only to preserve Aghora's carried-brain/self-impregnation lineage fact for No-Name, not a scene-usable peer persona.

peers.arc_label: Daughter of Baron Berard of Castaka, wife of Othon Von Salza—argues for Othon's rescue in vol1, dies defending clan honor in vol2
peers.honcho_notes: Daughter of Baron Berard of Castaka; married to Othon Von Salza per Berard's arrangement. Mother of Bari, who declared he wanted to die as she did. Knows the Epyphite secret by clan membership. Emotionally open in contrast to warrior stoicism Berard demands—wept at Berard's death; argued for saving Othon's life over secrecy. Willing to sacrifice herself for clan honor: walked alone to confront the invading force and was disintegrated at the base of a great column. Her death is called 'needless' by some but Bari frames it as heroic.
peers.rationale: Identical identity across both records: daughter of Baron Berard of Castaka, wife of Othon Von Salza, mother of Bari. The 'Lady' title appears in vol1 formal usage and is dropped in vol2. The underscore peer_card_id (lady_edna) is the old staged format. The edna record is the newer format and is canonical. Vol1 covers her alive and active (arguing in council, present at Berard's death); vol2 covers her death defending clan honor. One continuous person across both volumes.

peers.arc_label: Baron Berard of Castaka — Castaka noble appearing across early volumes
peers.honcho_notes: Merge: same person, cross-volume id drift. Prefer baron-berard-of-castaka as it carries the dynasty name.
peers.rationale: baron-berard-of-castaka (vol02) and baron_berard (vol01) are the same character extracted under two character_ids due to naming inconsistency between volumes. Both are single-record singletons with no phase split. 'baron-berard-of-castaka' is the more specific and complete identifier and should be canonical.

peers.arc_label: Othon's faithful servant, father of the unnamed daughter pair, later suicide victim
peers.honcho_notes: Male faithful servant/household associate of Othon and father of two unnamed daughters (Nan-Nan/Ohouya as called on p08). Preserve the daughters' paired attack as related non-peer lore evidence, not as a separate Honcho peer. Iku-Tta speaks in ominous metaphors, reports his daughters' tower attack, later commits suicide, and Othon uses that death to ban tribe members and replace household service with robots.
peers.rationale: Source correction from page images: vol.04 page 05 names the green servant as Iku-Tta and says 'my daughters'; vol.04 page 13 says Iku-Tta committed suicide and refers to his presence as the threat. Prior iko-itta/ik-uta records were OCR/extraction variants of Iku-Tta, not separate daughter/elder peers.

peers.arc_label: Small sardonic robot narrator, serves successive Metabarons across all volumes
peers.honcho_notes: Primary voice is sardonic oral historian with genuine emotional attachment to master. Breaks into dramatic hyperbole, mocks Lothar, can be physically coerced into compliance. Knows the full Castaka lineage from Othon forward. Functions change across volumes (surgical assistant, life-support host, combat bot) but narrative persona is constant.
peers.rationale: Despite occasional apparent deaths or shutdowns (vol12 self-destruction, forced disabling in vol05), Tonto is consistently the same small screen-faced robot: sardonic narrator, emotionally reactive, serves the current Metabaron as master. The vol12 destruction is followed by reconstruction. Voice and role are stable across all 16 source records—no contradictory TRAIT or VOICE facts arise from merging.

peers.arc_label: Larger robot companion and audience to Tonto's narration across all volumes
peers.honcho_notes: Speaks with procedural impatience; threatens memory-wipe or dismemberment to enforce compliance. Listens to Tonto's narration but constantly interrupts. Anti-romantic in vol11 ('love is a foolish human concept'); combusts from lust in vol16. Can manifest as devastating holographic form. Status-conscious.
peers.rationale: Lothar is consistently the larger, procedure-obsessed, impatient counterpart to Tonto. Role shifts between passive audience and active operator, and in vol17 he dominates Tonto ('Sir Master Lothar'), but the core identity—impatient robot who drives the frame narrative forward, clashes with Tonto, serves the Metabaron—remains stable. No contradictory TRAIT or VOICE facts across all records.

peers.arc_label: Othon von Salza — pirate heir through castrated Metabaronic founder
peers.honcho_notes: Merge: pure id-format duplicate. The 9-record merged card is the authoritative identity. Discard othon_von_salza.
peers.rationale: Two peer_card_ids for the same character, differing only in id format (hyphen vs underscore). Both share the alias 'othon von salza'. No phase or role split indicated. othon-von-salza is the 9-record merged card spanning vol01–10; othon_von_salza appears to be a duplicate staging artifact. Canonical: hyphen format (cleaner, consistent with other merged cards).

peers.arc_label: Shabda-Oud priestess as active mother, trainer, and self-sacrificing martyr
peers.honcho_notes: Commands rooms decisively; cold training doctrine ('duty above love'); rare flashes of maternal warmth reserved as reward. Last surviving Von Salza bloodline holder. Emits hypnotic waves; Aghnar eventually resists them. Self-sacrificial martyr who stays behind so family escapes. Her death is the foundational wound of Aghnar's revenge arc.
peers.rationale: Three-way split of Honorata records because each phase produces incompatible Honcho facts. This card covers her as a living agent: veiled arrival with Othon (vol03), active mother and exile trainer of Aghnar (vol04), sacrificial death by heart-bomb (vol05), and posthumous vengeance references (vol06–07). The living Honorata's VOICE is 'decisive commander who suppresses maternal feeling; duty above love.' The vol06–07 records are thin dead-person references but belong here rather than as a separate card because they describe the same persona's legacy.

peers.arc_label: Honorata who survived via time fissure—aged 20 years, manipulative, calculating strategist
peers.honcho_notes: Pushes Shabda-Oud psychic power beyond training limits; can open time fissures. Conceals survival strategically. Uses scent and private phrases as identity proof. Forces binary choice on Aghnar. Nightly appearance limited to ~30 seconds behind isolation requirement. Capable of chrono-temporal manipulation and deep psycho-surgery.
peers.rationale: After the apparent heart-bomb death, Honorata used Shabda-Oud time-acceleration to survive and age from 30 to 50 inside a time fissure. This is a fundamentally different operational phase: she deliberately concealed her survival from Aghnar for years, performed dangerous psycho-surgery on Oda, and forced a binary choice ('between Oda and me'). The VOICE here is 'calm, unapologetically calculating; argues that concealing emotion protected the family from hostile entities.' The vol12 record is the same temporal event (reaching the precise Pradex point) referenced mechanically. This persona cannot share a card with the living trainer because the manipulation and concealment contradict the martyr's sacrifice.

peers.arc_label: Honorata reincarnated inside Oda's body—merged identity raising Steelhead as warrior
peers.honcho_notes: Commands Steelhead to defend clan honor; publicly identifies as 'widow of Othon von Salza and mother of Aghnar von Salza.' Raises Steelhead as warrior capable of killing Aghnar. Accepts Aghnar's binary choice ('the Castakas must continue'). Voice of Oda's body but Honorata's will and doctrine. Ended via suicide mini-bomb with Aghnar in vol11 after Steelhead's treachery.
peers.rationale: Merges records from both character_ids 'honorata' and 'oda' because from vol09 onward the canonical description is 'Honorata's spirit within Oda's restored body'—these records describe the same composite entity. The vol09-10 'oda' records explicitly state Honorata supplanted Oda's identity. The vol11 'honorata' record describes her being mutilated and dying with Aghnar by mini-bomb as part of this merged body. Distinct from the living Honorata (active trainer) and the reborn Honorata (time-fissure strategist) because this persona's goal is raising Steelhead as warrior and she overrides the prior Aghnar/Oda pact against warrior succession.

peers.arc_label: Othon's passionate son—from council defiance to crippled warrior to mourned dead
peers.honcho_notes: Passionate and confrontational voice; equates glorious death with honor. Equestrian bond (Shazam the horse). Physically disabled from broken legs. Capable of genuine remorse and reconciliation with father. Deceased before vol04 events; present as object of mourning and inheritance reference only in later records.
peers.rationale: All four Bari records describe the same person: Othon's son. Vol01 shows him as infant/young defender; vol02 as crippled, volatile young adult who reconciles with Othon; vol03 as deceased mourned by Othon; vol04 as the 'faithful servant' whose daughters and horse remain with Othon—a post-death reference to the same figure. The vol04 designation 'faithful servant' is a translation artifact; the text describes Bari's daughters and horse, confirming the same person. No contradictory facts.

peers.arc_label: Loyal companion and southern assault commander who dies at Marmola
peers.honcho_notes: Loyal subordinate to Othon; twin of Hohenhole. Executed the southern assault via secret tunnels. Body recovered by Othon as a mark of honor. Not directly quoted in surviving pages.
peers.rationale: Both records clearly describe the same person: a warrior in Othon's household who appears near a white cubic structure in vol01 and leads the southern tunnel assault and dies at Marmola in vol02. Twin of Hohenhole. Thin records, no contradictory facts.

peers.arc_label: Distracted stone-cutter in vol01; northern assault commander in vol02; fate unconfirmed
peers.honcho_notes: Distracted register; must be redirected to focus. Twin of Konrath. Northern assault commander. Othon searched the northern battlefield for him after fighting ended—resolution not shown in surviving pages.
peers.rationale: Both records are the same person: Othon's lieutenant who is easily distracted (vol01) and leads the northern assault at Marmola with unconfirmed fate (vol02). Twin of Konrath. Thin records, no contradictions.

peers.arc_label: Princess Oda Capricious as an independent agent—before Honorata's reincarnation within her
peers.honcho_notes: Voice: 'That is not the blue rose I want'—unwavering public standards. Courageous under lethal threat; held blade to herself to coerce father. Willing co-conspirator in Aghnar's infiltration plan. Deeply emotionally attached; merges psychic energy with Aghnar 'united forever.' Left mentally devastated after the battle. Genetically unique—Shabda-Oud target her womb for their breeding plan.
peers.rationale: Separated from the Marmola Oda (different person) and from the Honorata-in-Oda records (vol09–10). In vol07–08, Oda operates with her own will: refuses suitors, holds a blade to herself to coerce her father, agrees to infiltrate the Shabda-Oud, tends Aghnar's wounds, merges psychic energy with him. She has a clear personal voice and agency. After vol08, Honorata's spirit supplants her identity. Keeping vol07–08 separate preserves Oda's distinct VOICE and TRAIT data for an authentic individual persona.

peers.arc_label: Sacred androgyne from imperial embryo to reigning empress across multiple generations
peers.honcho_notes: Conjoined-twin androgyne; biologically male and female simultaneously. Created after 30 years of effort on a hospital-planet. Messianic figure expected to unite all factions. Targeted by Shabda-Oud succession plot (Sama-Wajd prophesied to dethrone her). Commands Purple Endoguard. Rarely speaks directly in surviving pages—acts as political anchor rather than active voice.
peers.rationale: All records describe the same entity at different life stages. Vol03 is the embryo/sacred egg; vol04 is the named assassination target of the Oiders' plot; vol07–10 are the reigning empress of the galaxy. No direct voice exists in any record (vol10 has minimal implied agency). No contradictory TRAIT facts arise from merging—the entity transitions from embryo to ruler but remains consistently the target of dethronement plots and the political anchor of the galactic order.

peers.arc_label: Sterile Emperor who fathered Janus-Jana and bestowed the Metabaron title on Othon
peers.honcho_notes: Sterile; Janus-Jana produced after 30 years via scientific means. Expresses deep personal gratitude to Othon. Offers compassionate consolation ('another horse'). Rules jointly with the Empress. Grateful sovereign rather than commanding autocrat.
peers.rationale: Split from the Aghora-era Emperor because generations separate them—different people hold the same title. The Othon-era Emperor is personally sterile (required hospital-planet conception of Janus-Jana), emotionally attached to Othon, bestowed the hereditary Metabaron title. The Aghora-era Emperor (vol16) is described as 'two-headed'—visually and biologically distinct. Contradictory TRAIT facts if merged.

peers.arc_label: Two-headed Emperor who employs Aghora as mercenary—generations after Othon's Emperor
peers.honcho_notes: Two-headed or conjoined-headed figure. Has authority over entire Imperial Fleet. Politically pragmatic—accepted Aghora's terms after capability demonstration. Asked directly if she intended to kill him and take his place. Very thin record; primarily a contracting patron.
peers.rationale: Distinct from the Othon-era Emperor by both biology ('two-headed') and timeline. Accepts Aghora's solo contract terms after she demonstrates power by purging the court. Cautious pragmatist rather than emotionally attached patron.

peers.arc_label: The Empress who bore Janus-Jana and dispatched Honorata to Othon
peers.honcho_notes: Acts jointly with the Emperor in public appeals and court governance. Commands galactic-scale resources. Politically active in arranging rewards for exceptional service. Not directly quoted at length in surviving pages.
peers.rationale: Split from the later reigning Empress records. This Empress is specifically Janus-Jana's biological mother; her ovum was fertilized after 30 years on a hospital-planet. She also arranged Honorata as a reward-gift for Othon. Distinct role and era from the vol11–17 Empress who appeals to Steelhead and is protected by Aghora.

peers.arc_label: The Empress who appeals to Steelhead and is protected by Aghora—possibly Janus-Jana
peers.honcho_notes: Rules the empire from the Golden Planet. Vulnerable without the Metabaron's protection—this dependency structures her relationship to the Castaka lineage. Appealed to Steelhead in exchange for his demand for the Supreme Metabaron title. In vol17 described as 'exhausted from battle and recent childbirth.' Target of assassination attempts.
peers.rationale: These two records both describe a reigning Empress from the Golden Planet in the Steelhead–Aghora era. Vol11 Empress appeals to Steelhead for help against dimensional vampires; vol17 Empress is protected by Aghora and is under psychic assault. The timeline and role are consistent—both are the political sovereign seeking Metabaron protection. Likely the same individual (possibly Janus-Jana herself, though not confirmed). Merging is safe; contradictory facts would only arise if they were demonstrably different rulers.

peers.arc_label: Bald scarred Metabaron who is Tonto and Lothar's master throughout the frame narrative
peers.honcho_notes: Bald; distinctive scar over right eyebrow (origin deliberately withheld—'deplorable episode'). Self-described as 'a warrior without a past in the new galaxy.' Forceful, impatient with robot reasoning. Ruthlessly security-conscious: destroyed loyal servants to prevent enemies learning his secret. Calls robots his 'only friends.' Operates in another dimension; returns only for combat. Bio-electrogram manifestation dissolves in ~3 minutes.
peers.rationale: Both records describe the same bald figure who is Tonto and Lothar's current master. Vol03 shows the bald Metabaron manifesting as a bio-electrogram during the Metabunker assault. Vol12 shows the bald Metabaron with the right-eyebrow scar destroying the Metabunker and departing to another dimension—explicitly identified as 'the last of the Metabarons.' Tonto references the eyebrow scar mystery in vol07/11 as a deferred story topic, placing this character as the frame narrative's anchor throughout. This is Aghora's son No-Name.

peers.arc_label: Supreme Metabaron operating in Steelhead's time—identity explicitly unresolved in vol14
peers.honcho_notes: Relies on speed and maneuverability rather than brute force. Tactically precise—exploits turning radius as a time advantage. Protective of Milady; commands her to follow his exact path. Generates lethal spherical energy field. Addresses subordinates in guiding/commanding tone. Whether this is Steelhead in his Metabaron role or a distinct figure is unresolved.
peers.rationale: This record is explicitly flagged as uncertain whether it depicts Steelhead or a separate figure ('The Metabaron, Supreme Metabaron, Petro (possible)'). The vol14 narrative itself marks this as unresolved. Cannot safely merge with the No-Name Metabaron (different era) nor with the Steelhead card (unconfirmed identity). Split_uncertain because the source record's own analysis declares the identity open.

peers.honcho_notes: Merge: id-format variants plus spacing/OCR artifact. Three ids, one entity.
peers.rationale: Three ids for the same entity: the-technopope and technopope differ only in the definite article; the_techno_pope (vol01 single-record, underscore format) is the same character under an old extraction id. Fuzzy pair 'techno pope' / 'technopope' (ratio 0.952) confirms OCR/spacing variant. the-technopope is the cleanest and most complete canonical form.

peers.arc_label: Steelhead from grafted infant to prime Metabaron seeking love—before Krleza merger
peers.honcho_notes: Faceless/featureless head; head contains deadly weapons under helmets. Transactional—refuses altruism, demands payment. Prideful about combat supremacy. Emotionally volatile but admits openly he cannot love. Leveraged vampire crisis to demand Supreme Metabaron title. Searched 3,500+ planets for knowledge of love. Capable of stealth infiltration and assassination. Inherited Shabda-Oud psychic powers through mother.
peers.rationale: Three-way split of Steelhead records. This card covers his arc from infant (vol08, grafted on Tonto) through young champion (vol09) to active Metabaron (vol10, dueling Aghnar) to the pre-merger warrior seeking love (vol11). These form a coherent continuous persona: ambitious, militarily dominant, prideful, admits he cannot feel love, searches 3,500 planets. Distinct from the in-Melmoth phase (subsumed warrior component) and the post-Melmoth phase (all-Storlon, reverted pure warrior).

peers.arc_label: Steelhead's warrior ego as a subsumed internal personality after merger with Krleza
peers.honcho_notes: Internal warrior voice within Melmoth's composite body. Contemptuous of ostentation and romantic display; calls the heart-shaped wedding fleet 'a sign of impotence.' Interprets Metabarons as defined by suffering, not happiness. Demands body be used for combat. Associated with concealed electro-cerebral chips. Never fully dissolved into Melmoth—retained individual selfhood. In open war with Krleza at vol13's end.
peers.rationale: After the Endo-robot fusion with Zaran Krleza to form Melmoth, Steelhead ceases to be an independent actor and exists as an internal voice contesting Krleza for bodily control. Vol12 describes him as a subsumed component; vol13 shows him as the warrior internal personality at war with Krleza inside Melmoth's composite body. The active combatant persona is gone; what remains is a voice arguing for bodily control for battle. This is a fundamentally different state from the active warrior and requires a distinct Honcho card.

peers.arc_label: Steelhead re-emerged as pure warrior after killing the Krleza persona—all-Storlon body, defeats and loses to Aghora
peers.honcho_notes: Declared 'there is no love, only the reality of war.' Replaced entire body with Storlon indestructible metal; removed his own heart to erase grief over Dona Vicenta. Cold, commanding, emotionally void. Administered brutal initiation rites to Aghora. Chose female twin Aghora over male heir, fracturing succession rule. Preserved Dona Vicenta in omni-cryoshroud. Eventually defeated by Aghora's freezing weapon and sealed in deep space.
peers.rationale: The vol14 melmoth record describes someone who has killed the Krleza/Zaran internal persona and reverted to pure warrior identity—internally this is Steelhead, operating under the 'Melmoth' label. Vol15–17 records confirm this pure warrior phase: blue-faced, all-Storlon body, removed his own heart to erase grief. Fundamentally different from the in-Melmoth phase (contested composite) and from the pre-merger warrior (who sought love and had emotions). Using character_id 'melmoth' in vol14 for this record is a labeling artifact; the operational persona is Steelhead.

peers.arc_label: Composite being (Steelhead body + Krleza head) as theatrical romantic warrior pursuing Dona Vicenta
peers.honcho_notes: Describes himself as 'complete—a union of poet and warrior.' Speaks in elaborate devotional language to Dona Vicenta; frames massacres of 72,000 macromites as romantic gifts. Still tactically lethal despite emotional transformation. Seeks procreation to continue Metabaron lineage. Believes love can overcome murder and death. Privately distrusts public honors. Dual internal selves that cannot reconcile ultimately cause his breakdown.
peers.rationale: Vol11–13 records all describe the same composite Melmoth entity: warrior capability fused with poetic capacity, theatrically romantic in pursuit of Dona Vicenta, orchestrating atonement (cloning her father), marrying her, but undone by internal war between personas and the wedding-night disaster. Excludes vol14 where Melmoth has killed the Krleza persona and reverted to Steelhead.

peers.arc_label: The last poet — 5,000-year disembodied head, then poet component within Melmoth
peers.honcho_notes: Merge: OCR kr→kl transposition. zaran-krleza is canonical (correct spelling, authoritative 4-record card).
peers.rationale: zaran-klezra (vol15 single-record singleton) and zaran-krleza (4-record merged card spanning vol11–14) are the same poet entity. 'Klezra' is an OCR transposition of 'Krleza' (kr→kl metathesis, ratio 0.917). zaran-krleza is the authoritative merged card with correct spelling and four source records; zaran-klezra is a later extraction artifact with the transposed form.

peers.arc_label: Aghnar from weightless infant through brutal initiation ordeal to first combat on Okhar
peers.honcho_notes: Born permanently weightless; steel bracelets for grounding. Carries internalized total-distrust doctrine including distrust of mother. Exceptionally high pain tolerance from Shabda-Oud training. Defeated Honorata in combat; received only one kiss as reward. Metabaronic initiation rite canonized through his experience. At end of vol05: able to fight adult-level opponents, vows vengeance alongside Othon.
peers.rationale: Three-way split of Aghnar records. This card covers his formation as a character: born weightless from epiphyte exposure, raised in seven-year exile by Honorata, passed the robo-killer trial and foot-crushing ordeal, received prosthetic feet, defeated Shabda-Oud assassins. The voice in this phase is 'short determined utterances; I want to make my father proud; trust no one not even your mother.' Distinct from the adult revenge-arc warrior whose voice is emotionally complex and command-oriented.

peers.arc_label: Adult Aghnar executing revenge, winning Oda, then building family life—before aging into cold mercenary
peers.honcho_notes: Tactically brilliant—employs deception, psychic disguise, mind-control, concealed weapons simultaneously. Stoic about physical suffering but emotionally devoted to Oda and Honorata. Performed patricide on Othon as Castaka rite. Grafted Oko mini-bombs from Othon's corpse into himself. Won Oda via psychic blue-rose manifestation. Sacrificed arm as internal bomb to destroy Jejoh. Declared vengeance complete; wanted to cease being Metabaron and live as ordinary family.
peers.rationale: Vol06–08 form a coherent arc: adult Aghnar on Perdita in isolation, then executing the Shabda-Oud revenge, winning Oda's love, and post-revenge attempting family life. The voice is 'intense emotional investment when discussing revenge or family; commands with authority; tactically brilliant deception.' Despite the emotional complexity of vol08 (reunion with Honorata, Steelhead's birth), the core persona is consistent. Distinct from the child phase (formation) and the late-aged mercenary phase (vol10, emotionally cold, accepts genocide contract).

peers.arc_label: Aging cold mercenary Aghnar who accepts genocide contract, duels Steelhead, dies by mini-bomb
peers.honcho_notes: Emotionally cold, transactional mercenary. Adheres to warrior honor code—denounces dishonorable tactics as treason. Aging; notices own deterioration. Accepted Pthagurean genocide contract for payment. Won the Steelhead duel (Steelhead yielded honorably) before Steelhead's treachery cost him Honorata/Oda. Chose mutual mini-bomb suicide rather than capitulate. Final voice: sharp moral indignation ('bio-rat,' 'traitor').
peers.rationale: By vol10, Aghnar has aged visibly, publicly broke with the Empire (killing guards on departure), accepted a Pthagurean genocide contract, and is described as 'colder than a Venusian salmon's blood.' This is a dramatic shift from the vol06–08 warrior who wanted to retire and build family life. Vol11 shows his final combat against Steelhead and suicide by mini-bomb with Honorata/Oda after Steelhead's treachery. The emotionally cold mercenary voice cannot share a card with the emotionally invested revenge-warrior.

peers.arc_label: The Father-Mother Metabaron—from Steelhead's daughter to self-conceiving No-Name's parent
peers.honcho_notes: Bald, female-bodied, carries male twin's brain (transplanted by Steelhead). Raised and presented as male heir. Possesses bionic left hand from initiation rite; psycho-mimetic aura; invisibility cloak. Shed first tear only at Deyanira's death. Radically self-sufficient—fights alone, refuses fleet command. Performed first auto-conception in history via hypo-genetics from own brain tissue. Grieves that she can only destroy, not create, before choosing to have No-Name. Designated him 'No-Name' and 'father-mother.'
peers.rationale: All three records describe the same person at continuous life stages: vol15 shows childhood through defeating Steelhead; vol16 shows prime Metabaron, self-conceiving No-Name, departing to give birth; vol17 shows her pregnant and giving birth on Flos. The voice and traits are consistent throughout: resolute, mission-focused, duty-driven, despises humanity, governed by Bushitaka warrior doctrine. No contradictory facts.

peers.arc_label: Aghora's tarantuwolf companion—nursemaid, weapon, and only friend; dies of brain tumor
peers.honcho_notes: Large spider-like or multi-limbed non-human creature. Female. Loyal and affectionate toward Aghora. Capable of extreme violence—killed imperial troops and devoured the Technopope alive. Can be calmed by direct physical contact from Aghora. Died of a severe terminal brain tumor. Final act was an affectionate lick. Remains ejected into space via Paleo-Viking funerary ritual. Communicates through growls, howls, and physical gestures only.
peers.rationale: All three records describe the same creature: the tarantuwolf Deyanira, tamed by Aghora at age five. Vol15 thin reference; vol16 full account including killing the Technopope and death; vol17 recap of the same events. Merge straightforward.

peers.arc_label: The Grandmother — from Troglosocialik noble to Metabaronic matriarch
peers.honcho_notes: Merge: OCR alias collision plus old-format duplicate. dona-vicenta is the authoritative 5-record card.
peers.rationale: dona-vicenta (5-record merged card) and dona_vicenta_gabriela_de_rokha are the same character. The fuzzy pair 'do a vicenta' (ratio 0.967) is an OCR artifact of the same alias. dona_vicenta_gabriela_de_rokha uses old underscore format; dona-vicenta is the clean merged canonical. No phase or role split warranted.

peers.arc_label: The authentic Don Nicanor—Troglosocialik president, assassination target, dead before vol11 ceremony
peers.honcho_notes: Fanatically attached to traditions of nobility; sole ambassador who would never approve Steelhead's elevation. Practices calm morning meditation ritual among tiny birds. Identified as last planar Tay priest associated with traditional ecology. Enlightened, principled. Killed by Steelhead during morning meditation—a Cerebrak IK-8 shot. His remains were presented by Dona Vicenta at the ceremony as evidence of murder. His death is referenced in vol15 recap as the event that preceded Steelhead's rise and the war against the Techno-Technos.
peers.rationale: The vol15 singleton's sole witnessed fact—'death mentioned in recap as the event preceding Steelhead's rise and war against the Techno-Technos'—maps unambiguously to the original's assassination arc (vol10-11). Steelhead's rise follows the original's murder, not the clone's vol14 death during the castle assault. The vol15 record carries no body, voice, or trait data that would contradict the original's profile; it is a thin recap echo of the same killing event.

peers.arc_label: The cloned revival of Don Nicanor—publicly coherent but privately memory-unstable; eventually killed again
peers.honcho_notes: Commanding public orator: inspires large parliamentary crowds with ideological speeches. Post-revival: dangerous private memory instability—fails to recognize his own daughter in private while appearing coherent in public. Makes delusional romantic advances toward Aina Vicenta Gabriela. A trial of socialization was required before full public reintegration. In vol13 paternal memory is restored when he receives Vicenta's self-removed eye—overwhelmed with horror and remorse, weeps and begs forgiveness. Performs public dawn ecological meditation as federation president. Refuses Technoclergy bikramen ultimatum; Philodendra bombarded. Killed during the Metabaron/Petro castle assault in vol14.
peers.rationale: The vol13 record (don_nicanor_rosamel_de_rokha) explicitly labels 'Clone' as a trait—not an inference. It continues the vol12 clone arc directly: same memory instability toward Dona Vicenta, same clone origin via Melmoth, same political role as federation president. Paternal recognition is restored mid-vol13 by Vicenta's eye-sacrifice, then the same clone commands Philodendran forces in vol14 (still failing to recognize her initially) before being killed during the castle assault. The underscore character_id variant is a formatting artifact from extraction; the entity is identical to don-nicanor__clone.

peers.arc_label: Giant golden deity figure—power source of the Shabda-Oud, destroyed by Aghnar's bomb arm
peers.honcho_notes: Treated by Shabda-Oud as godlike and immortal. Giant golden humanoid. Externally impenetrable—vulnerable only from within. Central power source for all Shabda-Oud psychic abilities; their collapse when he is destroyed confirms this. Invoked as religious authority. Destroyed when Aghnar baited him into biting off a bomb-rigged arm.
peers.rationale: Both records describe the same entity: vol07 is the active encounter where Jejoh bites off Aghnar's arm and is destroyed by the concealed mini-bombs; vol08 is a recap reference to the same destruction. Straightforward merge.

peers.arc_label: Shabda-Oud hierarchy leaders / Mother Superior office across appearances
peers.honcho_notes: Group-role card for the Mother Superior office; keep separate from ordinary Shabda-Oud witches/priestesses.
peers.rationale: Project lore rule: Mother Superiors sit above the Shabda-Oud witches and should stay a separate hierarchy card rather than split by volume.

peers.arc_label: Recurring Shabda-Oud witches / whore-priestesses as an order-member group across eras
peers.honcho_notes: Group-role card for ordinary Shabda-Oud witches/priestesses/reverend mothers; encode general traits and group facts, not a single individual.
peers.rationale: Project lore rule: one, two, three, four, or more whore-priestesses/witches are recurring Shabda-Oud order members, not distinct peer personas.
